scope: Source-supported deprotected B1 glucoside attachment through the PheB1 N boundary atom. The insulin backbone beyond that nitrogen, including its N–Cα peptide continuation, is outside this component graph.

locations: Fig. 2a: NNC2215 product drawing, including the B1 glucoside connection.
Chemistry: O1-glucoside is attached through a short linker at the B-chain N-terminal amino group PheB1.
Methods, Synthesis of NNC2215: desB30 insulin is coupled at B1 with the peracetyl glucoside active ester; acetyl groups are removed by gentle saponification.

extended_data_figure_7b.location: Extended Data Fig. 7b, beta-carboxymethyl-oxyethyl-O-peracetyl-D-glucoside active ester. The figure labels the glucose carbons C1–C6; linker carbons are not assigned separate numeric source labels.

supporting_information.section_2: pp. 2–4: synthesis of beta-carboxymethyl-oxyethyl-O-peracetyl-D-glucoside active ester; H-1 doublet J=7.9 Hz; glucose and linker NMR assignments; peracetylated acid is converted to the active ester.
supporting_information.section_4: pp. 10–11: active ester coupling to B1 at pH 7.5, isolation of B1-O-peracetyl-glycoside, then saponification at pH 10.5 for 6 hours to the B1 glycoside.
supporting_information.mass_benchmark: §4, p. 11: following trypsin and TCEP treatment, glucoside is reported on the B1–B22 fragment at measured 1376.6 and calculated 1376.2 [M+2H]2+.

patent.location: Example 2 (INS2): B1 glycoside active-ester coupling to B29-alkyne insulin at pH 7.5, followed by sodium-carbonate saponification of the O-acetyl esters; see paragraphs describing INS2 and the B1-O-peracetyl-glycoside intermediate.

transcription.source_numbering: Glucose C1–C6 labels are retained from Extended Data Fig. 7b and SI NMR assignments. The linker is mapped by its depicted OCH2C=O and OCH2CH2O groups; no linker carbon numbering is invented.
transcription.linker_orientation: The glycosidic oxygen on glucose C1 connects to O–CH2–CH2–O–CH2–C(=O); the carbonyl carbon is attached to the PheB1 N endpoint.

evidence: Extended Data Fig. 7b depicts the beta-D glucoside and its glucose C1–C6 stereochemical substituent pattern.
SI §2 reports H-1 as a doublet with J=7.9 Hz, consistent with the beta-D-glucopyranoside anomer.
The detached sugar graph matches the beta-D-glucose reference structure (PubChem CID 64689; InChIKey WQZGKKKJIJFFOK-VFUOTHLCSA-N).
RDKit accurate CIP labels are used; RDKit documents its legacy CIP implementation as approximate and known to mislabel some centers.

1.role: Mapped protein-boundary placeholder for PheB1 N; it is joined to the B1 acyl carbonyl.
1.model_match_identity: Insulin B-chain PheB1 backbone N; this dummy is not included in substituent formulae or heavy-atom inventory.

2.role: B1 linker carbonyl carbon; amide carbonyl attached to PheB1 N.

4.role: Methylene alpha to the carbonyl; source NMR group OCH2C=O.

5.role: Ether oxygen between the carbonyl-alpha methylene and the ethylene linker.

6.role: First ethylene-linker methylene, adjacent to map 5.

7.role: Second ethylene-linker methylene, adjacent to the glycosidic-side ether oxygen map 8.

8.role: Glycosidic-side ether oxygen linking the ethylene linker to glucose C1.

9.role: Anomeric glucose carbon; beta-D glycosidic attachment site.

10.role: Glucopyranose ring oxygen between glucose C5 and C1.

11.role: Glucose C2 stereocenter bearing a free hydroxyl at map 12.

12.role: Free hydroxyl oxygen at glucose C2.

13.role: Glucose C3 stereocenter bearing a free hydroxyl at map 14.

14.role: Free hydroxyl oxygen at glucose C3.

15.role: Glucose C4 stereocenter bearing a free hydroxyl at map 16.

16.role: Free hydroxyl oxygen at glucose C4.

17.role: Glucose C5 stereocenter; bears the C6 hydroxymethyl substituent and ring oxygen map 10.

19.role: Free hydroxyl oxygen at glucose C6.

key_connectivity.role: PheB1 N–amide carbonyl C; map 1 is the N boundary placeholder.

operations: Replace the phenolic active-ester leaving group on the terminal acyl carbon with OH.
Remove the four O-acetyl protecting groups at glucose C2, C3, C4 and C6.
requested_graph_path.source_note: This is the normalized graph intermediate used for the formula and amide mass balance. The published NNC2215 procedure does not isolate this deprotected acid before protein coupling.

operations: Form PheB1 N–C(=O) bond; net loss of H2O from the acid plus insulin amino group.

published_procedure: The peracetylated active ester couples to insulin at B1 to give a peracetylated B1 glycoside amide.
Saponification then removes the four sugar O-acetyl groups to give the deprotected B1 glycoside.
transformations.active_ester_to_product_leaving_group: The active ester aryl-sulfonate group and its Br/CF3/sulfonate atoms are not part of the product graph.

composition.inventory_note: RDKit's mapped-dummy graph formula includes the side chain's 17 implicit hydrogens and a dummy atom. The net protein increment is one hydrogen lower because the PheB1 amino group loses one N–H as the amide bond forms.

sample_processing: Trypsin cleaves after ArgB22 to release the B23–B29 fragment from the B1–B22 fragment.
TCEP reduces insulin disulfides to separate A and B chains.
LC–MS assigns the glucoside to B1–B22; the reported 2+ ion is a peptide-fragment composition check, not a standalone mass measurement of the substituent.

rdkit_validation.stereochemistry_note: All five glucose stereocenters C1–C5 are assigned by RDKit accurate CIP; the detached sugar graph matches the beta-D-glucose reference InChIKey WQZGKKKJIJFFOK-VFUOTHLCSA-N. C6 is achiral CH2OH.
rdkit_validation.cip_method: RDKit accurate CIP implementation (useLegacyImplementation=False); legacy CIP is approximate and may misassign labels.

limitations: The PheB1 N endpoint is a mapped dummy placeholder whose model-match element is N; the insulin backbone is not included.
The B1–B22 fragment mass supports the modified-fragment assignment and composition but does not independently establish atom-by-atom coordinates.
The graph specifies neutral hydroxyls and an amide connectivity representation; it does not assign physiological protonation, charges, force-field parameters or a full-conjugate topology.
